At least 20% complete-work reduction in all six pairs is a promising synthetic cell. This is an engineering replication, not final statistical/resource/representative performance admission.

scope: Drawing omission produces repeatable complete-run gains when visual recording/raster work becomes material. Benefits vary with rendering load; no unrestricted compatibility or representative leadership claim.
limitations: No storage/network subset or discovery coverage.
Sampled process accounting and systemd resource limits do not establish final custody/resource admission.
Four synthetic density levels vary node count/paint complexity in a fixed viewport; not four independent real applications.

Complete-work time includes dynamic engine import, server/browser/context creation, navigation, every action and cleanup. Initial Bun/static-module startup and final result serialization are included only by observedOwnerMilliseconds.
Watchdog owner termination is observed at 100 ms polling granularity. Sampled CPU/RSS are diagnostic only; no final resource accounting claim.
Six independent pairs per engine/density describe the observed range; this does not establish population tails or representative real-application speedup.

inputManifest.scope: All tracked repository files plus selected private plan/controller/fixture/contract/wrappers, watchdog, driver, browser and Bun were hashed before and checked after every launch. Installed dependency bytes outside tracked source were not exhaustively captured.

conclusion: Painting exclusion is useful for the measured dense workload; lower-load behavior and all measured ranges are retained. This replication does not implement remaining capability categories or establish the majority-scenario 2x goal.
